title: Citi Forced To Inject Capital After Underestimating Risky Assets By $35 Billion
detail:
Citi Forced To Inject Capital After Underestimating Risky Assets By $35 Billion
Matias Civita
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 9:52 AM MST 3 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images

Citigroup underestimated its risk-weighted assets by approximately $35 billion after incorrectly recording certain trades at a European subsidiary, according to an exclusive Reuters report, forcing the Wall Street bank to inject additional capital into the business.

The error represents another setback for Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser as she works to resolve longstanding regulatory concerns surrounding the bank's internal controls, risk management and data governance practices.

According to people familiar with the matter who spoke to Reuters, the bank used an internal statistical model to calculate the risk associated with certain transactions at its British securities unit.

Regulators had not authorized the model for those types of trades. When the transactions were subsequently evaluated using a standard risk assessment model, the subsidiary's risk-weighted assets increased substantially.

Risk-weighted assets are an essential component of banking oversight because they determine how much capital financial institutions must maintain to absorb potential losses. An underestimation can result in a bank holding smaller capital buffers than appropriate for its exposure. Citigroup confirmed to Reuters that it had identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary during the summer.

"The subsidiary remained fully compliant with regulatory minimums throughout, with no impact on the holding company or main operating bank," Citigroup said. "Citi completed remedial actions and injected capital to immediately restore the subsidiary's buffers."

Citigroup, the third-largest U.S. bank by assets, reported approximately $1.2 trillion in risk-weighted assets in its June and September regulatory filings. The $35 billion discrepancy represented roughly 2.7% of its total reported risk-weighted assets, according to Reuters.

Reuters could not determine whether Citigroup had already incorporated the adjustment into its published financial figures. The discovery comes at a particularly sensitive time for Citigroup, which has spent years attempting to satisfy regulatory requirements imposed by U.S. authorities over deficiencies in its internal systems.

In 2020, the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ordered Citigroup to address longstanding weaknesses involving risk management, data governance and internal controls. The bank was fined $400 million in connection with those deficiencies.

Four years later, regulators imposed an additional $136 million in penalties after determining that Citigroup had failed to make sufficient progress in addressing its data management problems.

Key Takeaways

Citi downgraded McDonald's to Neutral from Buy on Nov. 18 and cut its price target to $301 from $315. The stock is 20% below its February high.

McDonald's U.S. comparable sales fell 0.2% in the third quarter on fewer guests, while Burger King's rose 8.4%.

Citi's $301 target is 10.5% above the Nov. 19 close. Applying today's 20.5x forward P/E to analysts' 2028 EPS estimate gives $297, within $4 of the target.

Citi looks right to step back because the multiple is already off its lows, and McDonald's targets a national launch of its new value program in early 2027.

McDonald's (MCD:NYSE) just lost one of its Buy ratings. Citi analyst Jon Tower downgraded the stock to Neutral from Buy on Nov. 18 and cut his price target to $301 from $315, a target he had raised from $295 after the third-quarter report.

That report had U.S. comparable sales down 0.2% on fewer guests. At Restaurant Brands International (QSR:NYSE), Burger King's U.S. comparable sales rose 8.4%. Yum! Brands (YUM:NYSE) saw Taco Bell's same-store sales fall 4% after a July food-safety outbreak, but CEO Chris Turner said on the Nov. 3 call that since the end of September the chain has been "outperforming the QSR industry on same-store sales growth." McDonald's says its restored digital offers beat expectations for extra visits, but it is still testing which value bundle to roll out nationally.

A Beat That Leaned on Selling Restaurants

McDonald's adjusted EPS rose 11% to $3.57, on revenue up just 1% to $7.16 billion. Other operating income, which includes gains on selling company-run restaurants to franchisees, rose to $139 million from $37 million. That $102 million was 43% of the $238 million rise in operating income, and higher gains on restaurant sales alone contributed $62 million.

On the call, Chairman and CEO Chris Kempczinski said U.S. comparable sales turned positive in September. His top priority is "nailing the final piece of our value equation, entry-level offerings," and McDonald's is testing value bundles in 1,900 U.S. restaurants ahead of a national launch targeted for early 2027.

Citi's Target Needs No Re-Rating

Citi isn't alone in cutting. The consensus target is $299, down from $332 a year ago and a $345 peak in March, so Citi's $301 sits just above the average.

MCD Stock Mean Price Target: 1-Year (TIKR)

Analysts expect normalized EPS of $12.94 this year, $13.65 in 2027 and $14.50 in 2028. The 2027 estimate was $14.00 three months ago.

MCD Normalized EPS: 2024-2028 (TIKR)

On 2028 estimates, $301 is 20.8x earnings, barely above today's 20.5x forward P/E and well below the five-year average of 24x.

The Easy Part of the McDonald's Rebound Is Done

The bigger long-term risk is NEXT. McDonald's plans about $8.5 billion of rent relief and capital support for franchisees through 2036. Rent relief comes straight out of franchised margins, which made up about 90% of McDonald's restaurant margin dollars in the third quarter.

Citi has the better side of this. The multiple has already climbed from 17x at its Sept. 30 low to 20.5x. If it stays there, further gains depend on higher forward earnings, and analysts have cut their 2027 estimate over the past three months. The fourth-quarter report is the next test: U.S. comparable sales have to grow against last year's 6.8% jump, and the 2027 outlook has to support the $13.65 a share analysts expect.

Can Bitcoin Reach Standard Chartered’s $500,000 Target by 2030?

Quick Read

Bitcoin needs an eightfold surge, about 698%, from roughly $62,700 to hit Standard Chartered's $500,000 target, and the author rates the odds low.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs bled $3.3 billion over 30 days, undercutting the long-term investors Standard Chartered counts on for its outlook.

Geoffrey Kendrick warned Bitcoin could fall to around $50,000 if the Federal Reserve keeps tightening, and a December 9 hike looms.

Standard Chartered's Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) target of $500,000 by 2030 is one of Wall Street's boldest forecasts. However, a significant drop in November has put that target further out of reach. The bank's analyst Geoffrey Kendrick confirmed this ambitious goal in April, but Bitcoin fell 11.8% in just a week, closing at a 90-day low of $62,997 on November 18.

Currently, Bitcoin trades around $62,685, down 50.3% from its all-time high of $126,080 set on October 6, 2025. Given ETF outflows and tightening Federal Reserve policies, how realistic is Standard Chartered's Bitcoin target?

Mindscape studio / Shutterstock.com
Bitcoin Needs a 698% Increase to Hit $500,000
William Potter / Shutterstock.com

To reach $500,000 from its current price, Bitcoin needs to appreciate about 698%, nearly an eightfold increase. Bitcoin's market value, or market cap, is calculated by multiplying the price of a single coin by the total number of coins in circulation, and it stands at about $1.26 trillion. If Bitcoin reached $500,000 with 20,113,584 coins in circulation, its market value would be around $10.06 trillion.

The potential supply could push that figure even higher. Bitcoin's design limits the total supply to 21 million coins. Miners continue to add new coins until this cap is reached, so more coins may be circulating by 2030. At the same $500,000 price, that could imply a market value exceeding $10.06 trillion. This also applies to its previous high, as $126,080 now represents a larger market value than in October 2025.

------

SoFi Active Invest is offering a limited-time promotion. Open an account, fund it with $50 or more, and you could receive up to $1,000 in complimentary stock for Active Invest accounts. See for yourself by clicking here now. (Sponsor)

------

Many advocates view gold as a standard for Bitcoin's value retention over time. However, gold is currently trading around $3,689 per ounce, down 30% from $5,279 at the end of February. Therefore, the benchmark that many forecasts, including the $500,000 call, rely on has also diminished.

Standard Chartered Already Pushed Its $500,000 Target to 2030
danielvfung / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

In December 2025, Standard Chartered revised its Bitcoin projections, moving the $500,000 target from 2028 to 2030. Its updated forecast includes interim targets of $225,000 for 2027, $300,000 for 2028, and $400,000 for 2029.

Kendrick confirmed again in April that the $500,000 target remains for 2030 and set a checkpoint of $100,000 for the end of 2026. However, he cautioned that Bitcoin could drop to around $50,000, a decrease of about 20%, if the Federal Reserve continues its tightening.

Reaching that initial checkpoint seems increasingly unlikely since Bitcoin needs a 60% surge to hit $100,000, and time is running out. Our analysis of Bitcoin's potential year-end position and its most plausible scenario for 2028 explores these nearer targets. Even Citigroup's (NYSE: C) relatively conservative target of $113,000, which ChatGPT, Claude and Grok each assessed in October, has a deadline of October 2027.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs Recorded $3.3 Billion of Outflows in 30 Days
24K-Production / Shutterstock.com

Standard Chartered indicates that long-term ETF investors are central to its outlook. Spot Bitcoin ETFs, exchange-traded funds that hold Bitcoin, purchase coins to back the shares sold to investors.

According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin funds reported $306 million in outflows on November 18 and $3.3 billion over 30 days. The funds still hold $77.7 billion in net assets, but the investors the bank relies on are more focused on selling than buying.

Additionally, many current holders face losses, with about half of the circulating Bitcoin acquired at prices above the current value, as per Glassnode data from November 17. These holders may sell during any potential recovery to cut their losses.

A Possible December Fed Hike Could Add Pressure on Bitcoin
Inspiration GP / Shutterstock.com

The federal funds rate, which the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending, directly affects borrowing costs. Higher rates tend to drive investors away from riskier assets like Bitcoin. In September, the Fed raised the upper limit from 3.75% to 4.00%.

Bitcoin reached a 90-day high of $86,597 on September 21, just days after the rate hike, but has since plunged 28%. Markets are bracing for another rate hike at the December 9 meeting, reinforcing Kendrick's warning of a potential drop to $50,000.

Is Bitcoin on Track to Meet Standard Chartered's $500,000 Target by 2030?

We believe Bitcoin has a low chance of reaching $500,000 by 2030. For this to happen, outflows from ETFs must reverse into steady inflows, and the Fed would have to halt its rate hikes. Bitcoin would also need to reclaim $100,000, surpass its all-time high of $126,080 (about 101% above its current level), and hit the bank's 2027 target of $225,000. That path requires an eightfold increase within four years.

If the Fed carries through with a rate hike on December 9 and outflows persist, Kendrick's $50,000 forecast could become a more likely near-term outcome. A close above the 50-day average of $78,600, an increase of about 25%, along with weekly ETF inflows after the decision, could revive hopes for the 2030 target. Conversely, closing the year below $100,000 would signal that the bank's initial checkpoint has already slipped out of reach.
